topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames complement as an important but nomenclaturally challenging subject and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement cascade fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual and molecular foundations for understanding complement as a cascade centred on C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3 convertase to cross the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes the elimination of pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activity to protect host cells from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains pathogen adaptations that impede complement and how one such adaptation, protein A, can be exploited clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
